title: Segregate ephemeral SNAT ranges per dedicated pool to prevent cross-tenant hostname reassociation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported intermittent tenant hostname misbinding after Dedicated GPU pool scale-up/scale-down events. Symptom: requests from tenant A intermittently resolved to tenant B's hostname for short windows (~30s-2m) following rapid autoscaler-driven container churn. Impact: customer-facing endpoints saw 500s or incorrect origin headers; manifested for hosted-style egress patterns and private VPC peered routes.
impact_summary: Occurs during Dedicated pool resize or failover when ephemeral SNAT (source port) ranges are reused aggressively by the egress NAT allocator, combined with long-lived L4 conntrack entries on shared NAT hosts. High-severity customer incidents opened by three enterprise customers in EU/US regions. Repro is intermittent but strongly correlated to scale events and bursty connection patterns.
repro_steps: 1) Provision two tenants (T-A and T-B) on a shared Dedicated egress host
2) Start high connection churn from both tenants (short lived connections to an external resolver that returns distinct A records per tenant origin),
3) Trigger Dedicated autoscaler to scale down and back up the pool (simulate churn),
4) Observe external DNS and HTTP logs for requests from T-A appearing with T-B's hostname or origin header within 30-120s window after scale event.
logs_and_signals: Conntrack timeouts show entries persisting longer than expected (60-90s beyond expected TTL)
SNAT port reuse mapping indicates allocator reassigning the same ephemeral port ranges across tenant namespaces within <1s
External resolver logs show mixed source ports and prior NAT mapping still servicing new source IP:port tuples
Customer HTTP request traces include inconsistent X-Forwarded-Host values during the window
root_cause_analysis: The allocator for ephemeral SNAT ranges on Dedicated egress hosts was optimized for minimizing port fragmentation (aggressive reuse). During scale-down/up this caused a small window where an old conntrack entry (source IP:port -> backend mapping) was still active while the allocator reassigned that same port to a different tenant namespace. The reuse plus asymmetric conntrack cleanup timing produced transient cross-tenant egress mapping. Persistent DNS caches and external resolver heuristics amplified the visible impact.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix v1: Introduced a short cooldown (120s) before reassigning ephemeral SNAT ranges after they are released by a tenant namespace. Deployed to eu-west-1 and us-east-1 egress hosts as a staged rollout.
Customer workaround: temporarily increase Dedicated pool min-size to avoid rapid scale-to-zero events; advise clients to flush resolver caches if they observed incorrect host mappings.
Added dashboard alerts for rapid port-reuse rates and conntrack aging anomalies (console-2026.03)
code_changes: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-nat/pull/874 - allocator: add cooldown window and namespace affinity tags
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/egress-agent/pull/439 - conntrack cleaner: prioritize namespace-scoped expirations and emit metrics
Config change: default cooldown set to 120s (config map: egress-nat.cooldown_seconds = 120)
rollout_plan: Canary on 10% of egress hosts in eu-west-1 -> monitor alerts for 2 hours -> expand to 50% -> monitor 24h -> full global rollout. If duplicated errors increase >1% of baseline within canary, rollback immediately.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: conntrack-age percentile by tenant namespace
postmortem_notes: Preliminary RCA points to an optimization tradeoff that favored port utilization over isolation safety. Longer-term plan includes namespace-bound ephemeral pools and enhanced invariants in conntrack cleanup. Recommend retro with Runtime team to replay scale events in staging harness and extend chaos tests to include rapid pool churn.
qa_and_validation: Integration test added: e2e/egress/snat_namespace_isolation_test (simulates 10k short-lived connections during scale events)
Load test: synthetic tenants run on staging for 48h with autoscaler enabled; verified zero host mix incidents
Security review: Kelsey Chen completed compliance check for SNAT changes (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/egress-snat-security)
